title: Course frontier: consistency and Spark preview
summary: Use the overview's later-course map to connect consistency testing, Spark data movement, MLlib, and cloud workflows without pretending missing lectures were supplied.
objectives: Separate the supplied overview from later lecture detail
Map a project question to consistency or shuffle evidence
Identify what source must be added before claiming full lecture coverage

sections.title: Scope boundary
sections.body: The supplied Lec0 overview names consistency models, Apache Spark, distributed algorithms, MLlib, and cloud computing as later topics. It is safe to use this page as a course map; detailed derivations require the corresponding lecture sources when they are available.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The examinability signal here is the official course roadmap, not an invented replacement for missing later slides.

sections.title: Preview a shuffle boundary
sections.body: A map or filter can often remain partition-local, while grouping, joins, and global sorts usually require data movement. Treat this as a study hypothesis to test against the Spark lecture and project implementation, not as a complete Spark derivation.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The preview bridges the clock-and-ordering foundations to future Spark work while preserving the source boundary.

examples.title: Evidence request for the next module
steps: State the claimed consistency or performance property.

examples.answer: The Atlas should distinguish a roadmap pointer from a fully taught derivation.

contrastDrills.prompt: Which operation usually requires records to move between partitions?
contrastDrills.explanation: Grouping by key brings records with the same key together and typically requires a shuffle.
contrastDrills.misconception: Name the ordering, time, or communication boundary before choosing.

choices: Label it as a roadmap/context pointer
Copy a generic answer without a source
contrastDrills.explanation: Keep the roadmap pointer visible and mark detailed coverage pending until the appropriate lecture or official source is available.
contrastDrills.misconception: Name the ordering, time, or communication boundary before choosing.

math.explanation: Map-like operations can often stay partition-local, while joins, group-bys, and global sorts may require a shuffle. The equation forces the experiment to name the data movement and synchronization costs instead of treating the pipeline as one opaque step.
math.name: Distributed-pipeline cost model
math.purpose: Use it to separate partition-local work, shuffle, and barrier waiting when comparing implementations.

math.explanation: Use this as a bridge from the course overview to Spark experiments: local computation, data movement, and coordination should be measured separately.
math.name: Distributed-job cost decomposition
math.purpose: Use it to measure compute, shuffle, and coordination as separate contributors to job time.
math.caveat: This is a derived study model; the supplied overview names Spark but does not provide the later lecture derivation.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why should this lesson be labeled a course frontier rather than full Spark coverage?
criticalQuestions.angle: Check which source pages are actually supplied.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Lec0 gives the roadmap and project direction, but the detailed Spark, consistency, and MLlib lectures are not in the current local source set.

criticalQuestions.prompt: What evidence would turn a shuffle hypothesis into a measured claim?
criticalQuestions.angle: Move from a conceptual operation to an instrumented stage-level observation.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Record partition sizes, shuffle bytes, task skew, stage time, and the logical operation that caused the exchange.
